actual.value:
Frankfurt School of Finance and Management executive course called Certified Expert in Climate Change Adaptation Finance, CECAF identified as suitable to address the identified climate adaptation finance knowledge gap in the Uganda environment. Course has been customised to a 75 hour version of the original 150 hour curriculum and cases from the East African rural and financial environment with a focus on Uganda added to develop a Climate Adaptation Finance Professional (CAFS) course. The project funded a main part of the course development costs while the curriculum development, examinations, certifications, and overall quality control have been handled by the Frankfurt School. The first two course cohorts will be subsidised by the project with Danish grant. Thereafter, the course is expected to run sustainably at around US$ 1,053 (EUR 950) per trainee. The course was promoted to be launched in October 2024 once the main ARCAFIM commenced. The course emphasises the following four topics:
(1) Addressing market imperfections related to adaptation finance to achieve efficient adaptation outcomes. (2) Building a business case for adaptation, including a new adaptation business model, or adjusting existing business models to increase climate resilience of portfolios. (3) Financial instruments, including financial tools to reduce adaptation risks and strategies for understanding and managing these risks. (4) Measuring, Reporting, and Evaluating Adaptation, including monitoring initiatives, managing risks and using indicators to inform adaptation investment decisions.
IFAD, with the Frankfurt School, plan to replicate the course in other ARCAFIM countries. EBRD and the Global Centre on Adaptation have shown interest and discussed with IFAD and the Frankfurt School to use part of the curriculum for other African countries.
During this ARCAFIM Pilot extension period, the project worked with EBUL on CCA Loans pipeline development in EB in Uganda, identified potential borrowers and appropriate lending channels for financing different CCA options. To further support this activity in Equity Bank, events were organised, consultants recruited, and various partnership arrangements arranged with key stakeholders and financial value chain partners. Detailed achievements are elaborated under output 4.

- ARACFIM Pilot Project closely cooperated with the Climate Finance Unit of the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development to develop the Uganda National Green taxonomy. Specifically, the ARCAFIM Pilot Taxonomy Framework Note and Compendium together with the aBi Green Taxonomy formed the joint green taxonomy that was integrated into the draft Uganda National Green Taxonomy for the Agriculture.
- During the Uganda-Denmark Partnership Day and launch of the new ARCAFIM (CCA support programme) in June 2024, IFAD team together with Equity Bank Uganda Limited (EBUL) provided information to other Danish Embassy partners on ARCAFIM programme and the prospective availability of CCA financial products at EBUL. Collaborations with aBi Finance and aBi Development and the potential anchor leads were further explored when the implementation of the main ARCAFIM programme commences.
- ARCAFIM Pilot and aBi Finance have planned wholesale funding activities targeting largely an overlapping client base and that require a similar reporting mechanism. Thus, discussions about the automated reporting database that aBi commissioned and is currently rolling out with its partner FIs was held between IFAD and aBi Finance. It was observed that the substantial and growing portfolio of aBi Finance indicated high demand in the market for CCA wholesale finance and generally low default rates for borrowing SACCOs. An opportunity for joint promotion and awareness campaigns for the demand side of the CCA finance in Uganda during the next phase of the main ARCAFIM project to start soon.
- A new Supplementary Funds Agreement for the next phase of Danish support of CCA finance and ARCAFIM implementation in Uganda signed in 2023 became operational following completion of the pilot. Lessons learnt during the Pilot Project were instrumental and leveraged during activities and budgets designing for this new Danish support.

title.narrative: Output 1. Readily available data on climate change relevant for Agriculture Finance.
1. Mapping of the ecosystem of meteorological service providers. 2. Report on Uganda climate information, risks, and projections relevant for agriculture CCA.

target.value: - Report on Uganda climate information and risks relevant for agriculture CCA completed.

actual.value: - Beside the climate studies conducted between October 2022 to end of 2023, an additional study on ARCAFIM Adaptation Finance Environmental and Social Risks and Management Framework (ESMF) conducted by Advance Consulting as a core component of the design package submitted to ARCAFIM financiers. The study provided a basis for the development of appropriate climate finance products, and their inclusive targeting measures, as further described under Output 4.

target.value: -Outdated or weak local information on climate change and climate variability relevant for climate adaptation within the agricultural sector.

actual.value: IFAD commissioned a study to map climate change risks and adaptation options in Uganda.

target.value: - Mapping of the ecosystem of meteorological service providers completed.

actual.value:
Thorough agriculture climate adaptation stakeholder mapping in Uganda conducted and in partnerships with a select organizations active in climate change assessment in Uganda and East Africa, the project developed several collaborations particularly in undertaking climate risk and vulnerability assessments among others. These included:
- A study to map climate change risks and adaptation options in Uganda completed. It analysed change in actual and projected temperature and precipitation, based on the sixth IPCC reports. Furthermore, the study analysed primary production systems at value chain level for crops, livestock and fisheries, identified vulnerabilities to climate change in the production systems and finally mapped out adaptation measures that respond to those vulnerabilities. The study was annexed to the ARCAFIM full draft Funding Proposal to GCF, Denmark, Finland and the Nordic Development Fund, to guide funding decisions by these Nordic donors and the GCF. The study results also formed part of the CCA taxonomy background package annexed to the ARCAFIM Operations Manual for Equity Bank.
- Climate Information Studies completed in partnership with the IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC) that collaborates with the Uganda National Meteorological Authority (UNMA) in their Agricultural Climate Resilience Enhancement Initiative-program. The studies also indicate that UNMA is supported by USAID Feed the Future to produce various longer-term forecasts for agricultural use or disaster preparedness. Financial and technical assistance is also provided to UNMA by GIZ and UNDP. Through these studies, ARCAFIM also established that while UNMA collected data and produced reports focused on short term weather advisory services, there was limited and insufficient focus on long term climate predictions valuable in strategic climate adaptation investments decision making.
- Mapping of the ecosystem of meteorological service providers also identified that Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK) in partnership with GIZ and BMZ implemented a programme on Climate Risk Analysis for SSA countries that conducted Climate Risk profiles that provide a condensed overview of present and future climate impacts and climate risks at national level for relevant sectors in partner countries. two value chains in Uganda were coffee and maize, their Climate Risk Analysis (CRA) findings were shared during a workshop that ARCAFIM team participated in. While the CRA on maize was applauded because it underlined the importance of new seed varieties and improved storage bags as adaptation strategies with consistently high IRRs, the analysis on coffee was received with more scepticism during this workshop. Specifically, the two adaptation strategies chosen; agroforestry and storage, were not considered the most obvious ones by stakeholders. The model for coffee did not project the impact of these strategies on coffee yield just on additional income from agroforestry and reduced harvest losses. ARCAFIM to explore the how to expand this CRVA methodology by PIK to other value chains and adaptation strategies moving forward.
- IFAD through the IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC), based in Nairobi collaborated with the Uganda National Meteorological Authority (UNMA) in their Agricultural Climate Resilience Enhancement Initiative program to further inform the conducted climate information studies.

actual.value:
Joint ARCAFIM/aBi Finance green taxonomy encompassing both mitigation and adaptation elements completed and informed the national green taxonomy for agriculture developed in collaboration with GoU through the Climate Finance Unit of the MoFPED. - Together with aBi Finance, a Taxonomy Compendium/Report on key studies and analysis on CCA taxonomy with details of eligible CCA investment options for small-scale crop, livestock and aquaculture producers, as well as agribusiness enterprises engaged in inclusive agriculture value chains and food systems has been completed. It groups the investment options according to climate risk type and includes recommendations of appropriate, viable combinations of CCA solutions for regions with different climatical conditions.
- Building onto work with aBi Finance, a joint taxonomy has been developed, it contributed to the Uganda National Green Taxonomy for agriculture that will be submitted to GoU cabinet for approval once the taxonomy for other sectors prioritised in the national Updated NDC have been completed as well. Together with aBi Finance, ARCAFIM team were part of the National Steering Committee that are peer reviewing and contributing to the development of this overall national green taxonomy.

title.narrative: Output 4. Loan products and lending methodology development

target.value: Dedicated CCA lending products available in FIs in Uganda

actual.value:
- A multidisciplinary team led by the Executive Director of public sector and social investments and comprising of managers from Product Development, Risk, Finance, Marketing and Operations Departments assembled at EBUL Kampala Head Office level.
ARCAFIM project publically launched, a Pilot Project budget and work plan for activities with Equity Bank Uganda agreed upon with IFAD, and the implementation significantly gained momentum. - Completed baseline assessment of ESG policy and its existing green products in EBU - Organized a sensitization workshop on climate change adaptation with EBU staff - Briefed EBU department heads on needs for CCA lending product development - Briefed EBU executive committee, including Managing Director, on the ARCAFIM programme.
An assessment undertaken by Equity Bank staff indicated that specific loan products for CCA do not yet exist among the portfolio of Equity Bank operations in Uganda. However, through the current products that EBUL offers, e.g. for (female) farmers or for MSMEs, there are many examples of loans for investments in or upgrading of assets that would qualify as CCA loans and only require a structure to earmark them for monitoring and reporting. Case examples include water management, irrigation systems, shading nets and post-harvest processing in the value chains of coffee, tea, beans, banana, casava, potato, vanilla, sesame, maize and soja beans
Pro-active use of alternative lending channels and data sources to increase outreach and to reduce lending risks identified and proposed as the approach for EBUL to develop a CCA pipeline and undertake loan origination. To collect lender data, active use of anchor companies and institutions was deemed important. Because anchors provide additional information for groups of prospective clients, and EBUL can operate more efficiently if it gathers this anchor data in a system that evaluates agri-loan applications. Various sub-sectors anchor companies can also be used as wholesale borrowers that on-lend the funds in cash or kind to smallholders for CCA investments, particularly in case of outgrower schemes based on assessments conducted.
It was also identified that Equity Bank Uganda has also issued wholesale loans for on-lending to SACCOs and MFIs that operate with large numbers of rural producers and micro-companies. Two rural SACCOs visited by the project team to gauge interest and demand for climate adaptation wholesale funds from EBUL. The observations confirmed that well-organised SACCOs can become significant lending channels under ARCAFIM, especially if their capacities are enhanced through TA resources of ARCAFIM.

target.value: - CCA Loans Pipeline Developed entailing documenting the cycle for CCA loans to identify and address any workflow glitches, demonstrating readiness for ARCAFIM - Frankfurt School of Management and Finance contracted to offer the Certified Expert in Climate Adaptation Finance (CECAF) course to Equity Bank Uganda and other appropriate Ugandan financial institutions - 2 sensitisation courses to EBUL field staff on climate change and CCA finance organised. - 3-day training sessions for all ARCAFIM field implementers in EB Uganda branches organised once key ARCAFIM legal and financing agreements have been signed. - consultants to support with climate change adaptation finance product development, pipeline development, and monitoring and evaluation for Equity Bank contracted since these are key interfaces between the Uganda pilot and the regional operations of ARCAFIM East Africa.

actual.value:
Activities during the Pilot Project extension period aimed to ensure that Equity Bank Uganda was fully equipped for the launch of main ARCAFIM. (a) As part of CCA Loans Pipeline Development, below actions taken to demonstrate ARCAFIM readiness and to address workflow processes.
Staff Orientation to CCA Loans. A comprehensive sensitisation initiative conducted and engaged 432 branch staff in 27 EBUL branches across all regions of Uganda. Through this initiative, awareness raised about ARCAFIM and climate adaptation finance while orienting staff on the importance of beginning to engage with potential agricultural anchors, including cooperatives and agri companies.
Engagement with Agricultural Anchors: Structured interviews with 27 potential agricultural anchors conducted to develop a robust pipeline for CCA loans under ARCAFIM. The process introduced the anchors to financing opportunities that ARCAFIM offer and documented various financing options within agriculture, agro-business, and livestock farming at the branch level.
Engagement with agro-companies and CSA Technology Providers: A comprehensive engagement initiative conducted to connect EB and ARCAFIM with agricultural companies, cooperatives, and Climate Smart Agriculture (CSA) technology suppliers in Northern Uganda, Western Uganda, West Nile, and Southwestern Uganda. 191 farmer groups, 20 agro-companies, and 25 CSA technology suppliers engaged during this outreach activity. As a result, 21 potential candidates among agro firms and technology suppliers identified and documented for CCA financing.
Partnership with the Cooperative Consortium: Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) successfully finalised with the Uganda Cooperative Alliance (UCA), Uganda Central Cooperative Financial Services (UCCFS), and Uganda Cooperative Savings and Credit Union (UCSCU). These strategic partnerships will enable EBUL to leverage these cooperative bodies for comprehensive capacity building and training of their member SACCOs on CCA finance. This collaboration set the stage for utilising the cooperative networks to disseminate CCA loan products through wholesale lending channel.
(b) In line in Output 2 above, where the Certified Expert in Climate Adaptation Finance (CECAF) Course as identified and customised to Uganda and the East African region broadly, EB team will nominate 16 senior staff members from EBUL for the CECAF course offered by the Frankfurt School in collaboration with MUBS once the main ARCAFIM is operational and the course delivered in July 2024.

target.value: No dedicated CCA lending products in Uganda.

actual.value:
Meetings between EBUL and IFAD held to plan for the pilot activities. Proposed activities majorly oriented towards enhancing EBULs retail activities. These included. (1) Training of EBUL staff in climate risk analysis capabilities and strategies, including capacity to assess physical and transition risks. (2) Testing the cycle for CCA loans i.e. promotion, pipeline build-up, loan assessment, disbursement, and collection, reporting and monitoring. Aimed at revealing any glitches in the workflow and ultimately demonstrates the readiness for ARCAFIM. (3) Engaging with agritech and or fintech companies and others anchors in the lending process to a) reduce cost of lending, and or b) improve the information available for lending, in making CCA loans to small producers and agri-MSMEs. () Developing systematic reporting and monitoring platforms/tools on ESG for ARCAFIM and its funders. 5) Generate lessons learned and ultimately a better starting position for EBUL to launch ARCAFIM and replicate its modalities and practices to other Equity Bank subsidiaries across ESA region.
A multidisciplinary team at EBUL Kampala Head Office assembled, led by the Executive Director of the public sector and social investments. This team comprised of managers from the Product Development, Risk, Finance, Marketing, and Operations Departments and will be responsible for planning ARCAFIM Pilot activities leading to the start-up of actual CCA lending operations by early 2025.
Discussions also held between Equity Bank Group and IFAD regarding strategy for rolling out CCA finance resources. Four distribution channels agreed upon; (a) two wholesale channels, through FIs or through VC lead companies, (b) two retail channels, to micro borrowers and to SME borrowers. Agreement reached for SME retail to be capped at 30% of total loan volume. This was to enforce the small producers and financial inclusion of the most vulnerable clients as well as the expected implementation of ARCAFIM wholesale channel since micro retailing is financially less attractive for EBU.
Due diligence process of Equity Bank Group for ARCAFIM conducted in the last quarter of 2022 and, its Uganda subsidiary was heavily involved in the process.
